label: Codex-gpt-5.6-sol-reviewer2-fulltext-2026-10-03

country.paper_says: The study examined “the provision and management of safe drinking water in rural Tasmania, Australia.”

study_design.paper_says: “Semi-structured interviews formed the basis of data collection,” and the researchers used a qualitative approach and thematic analysis.

population.paper_says: Interviews involved “12 local government representatives” from rural Tasmanian municipalities who “had public health responsibilities for the management of drinking water within their municipality.”

sample_size.paper_says: The paper reports interviews with “12 local government representatives”; the first extractor left sample size blank.

urban_rural.paper_says: The interviews were conducted with representatives “from each of the rural local government municipalities in Tasmania.”

service_provider.paper_says: In most rural and remote areas, “the provision and management of drinking water and the protection of public health is the sole responsibility of local government.”

regulatory_model.paper_says: Tasmania made the microbiological provisions of the Australian Drinking Water Guidelines statutory under the Public Health Act (1997). Water providers must regularly test supplies and report annually to the Director of Public Health, including non-compliant results; participants also described liability and accountability concerns.
regulatory_model.where: pp. 2–5, Background to the issue; Inadequate water distribution systems, treatment and resources

effect_measure.paper_says: “A thematic analysis was undertaken to interpret the interviews,” including identification and categorisation of emerging issues into themes.

effect_estimate.paper_says: The 12 interviews identified inadequate infrastructure, limited finances and staffing, testing costs, liability concerns, and competing land uses as barriers. The paper reports 30 boil alerts, 29 in rural municipalities; three participants considered shutting down supplies; one said “let’s cut the pipe, let’s stop the supply”; another cited “$1347 per test” for one herbicide.
effect_estimate.where: pp. 3–6, Findings and discussion—Inadequate water distribution systems; Protecting water sources; Adequate resources

extraction_note.paper_says: The supplied paper is identified in the review prompt as record RA1109B58A443.
extraction_note.where: Review record metadata supplied with paper

parsed.overall_comment: The extraction is substantively supported by the paper, except that sample size was omitted despite the paper clearly reporting 12 participants. The effect estimate accurately summarizes the qualitative findings and reported descriptive counts.
